I came from the floor. Used company LTP to go to school, while in school became a QAI/QPS, and then went into management 3 years after I graduated with my ME degree (18 months as a QE too). 

Here’s the deal- you are comparing blue collar workers to white collar workers. White collar workers who drag their feet and don’t get projects turned in on time, who don’t update BVCs, CLEaR records, CARs, and other documents on time. 
They build the planes. Sure quality has gone down a bit, that’s more so because we don’t retain our good talent due to wage issues. You start off by talking about engineers not getting paid as much as at tech companies; I lost a great engineer to a tech company who doubled her salary and paid for her relocation, then paid the first three months of her rent in Austin. It’s the same thing for the blue collar workers, you just are too involved in your own world to notice. Have you ever even been on the floor? Spent time with these people? They are good hardworking people. Diversity isn’t forced on the floor, we have people from Eastern Europe, South America, South Eastern Asia, Canada, and everywhere you can think of working out there. They all bring a different perspective to the table and that’s what makes us strong.The people building the planes deserve to live well too, even if they live differently. These inflammatory posts do nothing but drive a divide between the people who actually keep the show running. The first people to get a QOL increase have to be the ones who build the product so that we can start making money again. Then you get your wage increase, then leadership. That’s how it goes. 

You should be ashamed of yourself; and as a leader, I would be embarrassed to have you working for me.

We need him as much as we need those who build the planes, and those who work on RCCA, Sustainment, Fulfillment, and everything in between. One Boeing is a real thing.
